pr.title: Make inliner cycle detection a fallible process
pr.description:
The query `mir_callgraph_cyclic` is supposed to find _all_ callees that _may_ lead to a recursive call back to the given `LocalDefId`. But that query was built using a function which recurses through the call graph and tries to locally handle hitting the recursion limit during the walk. That is wrong. If the recursion limit is encountered, the set may be incomplete and thus useless. If we hit the recursion limit the only correct thing to do is bail.

Some benchmarks improve because for some functions we will bail out of the call graph walk faster. Some benchmarks regress because we do less inlining, but that is quite rare with the default recursion depth.

Originally I thought this might be a fix for https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/131960, but it turns out that it is _actually_ a fix for https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/146998.
pr.author: saethlin

evidence: Make inliner cycle detection a fallible process

// Pessimistically assume that there could be recursion.

analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical incorrect behavior was to keep returning and consuming a cycle-callee set even when the call-graph DFS had been cut off by the recursion limit: `process`/`mir_callgraph_cyclic` treated the partial result as if it were complete, and the inliner could therefore inline a callee whose path back to the caller was never explored. The local "pessimistic true" for one depth-limited branch did not make the global set complete. The correct transformation is not merely the new `/ 8` budget: on limit exhaustion the recursive result must become `None`, propagate via `?`, and `check_mir_is_available` must return `Err("call graph cycle detection bailed due to recursion limit")` rather than inline from an incomplete set.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR inlining under `-Zmir-opt-level=2 -Zinline-mir` (and `-O`) of functions with deep or broad call graphs, including generic wrapper functions and trait-method calls across a crate boundary, where the caller/callee relationship is potentially cyclic and the cycle-detection DFS exceeds the recursion limit. A focused pair should contain a deep call graph with a potentially cyclic callee reachable only beyond the cut-off depth.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the fix, `mir_callgraph_cyclic` returned `&'tcx UnordSet<LocalDefId>` and `process` returned `bool`. While walking transitive callees, if the recursion limiter did not permit further recursion, the code locally used the comment "Pessimistically assume that there could be recursion." and returned `true`; the walk then still produced an `UnordSet`. The query comment claimed the set contained all transitive callees that may lead back to the root, and `check_mir_is_available` used `mir_callgraph_cyclic(caller).contains(&callee)` to decide whether to avoid inlining. The recursion budget was `tcx.recursion_limit() / 2`.
pitfalls: An incomplete cyclic-callee set is not safe to consume: missing a callee means the inliner may inline a call that participates in a cycle.
Locally returning `true` for the branch that hit the recursion limit does not repair completeness of the overall set.
Only bailing from `process` is insufficient; the fallibility must propagate through the query return type and be honored by the inliner.
Changing the recursion limit from `/ 2` to `/ 8` alters how often bailout occurs but does not by itself fix the incomplete-set semantics.
Do not describe the new test as proving a specific MIR diff: it is marked `skip-filecheck` and is a compile-level regression test.
preconditions: The Inline pass is evaluating whether a callee may transitively call back into the caller.
The caller's transitive call graph is deep enough to exhaust the cycle-detection recursion budget.
A potentially cyclic callee lies beyond the depth at which the walk is cut off, so a partial set can omit it.
analysis.summary: Make MIR-inliner cycle detection fallible: `mir_callgraph_cyclic` must bail (return `None`) when its call-graph walk exhausts the recursion limit, and the inliner must refuse to inline instead of trusting a partial set of cyclic callees. This is a confirmed fix for rust-lang/rust#146998.
analysis.testStrategy: The patch adds a compile regression test `tests/mir-opt/inline/recursion_limit_prevents_cycle_discovery.rs` with an auxiliary `tests/mir-opt/inline/auxiliary/wrapper.rs` generic `wrap`/`Compare` API, compile flags `-Zmir-opt-level=2 -Zinline-mir`, and 65 macro-generated `Compare` implementations to force the recursion limit; it is marked `skip-filecheck` and explicitly says it is a regression test for issue 146998. For differential testing, construct two programs differing only in whether the deep cycle-detection walk bails or returns the partial set, and verify the bailing variant does not inline across the unexplored cyclic path. No compiler was built here and no execution or reproduction is claimed.
analysis.trigger: The recursion limit is encountered while `mir_callgraph_cyclic` walks callees during the inliner's `check_mir_is_available` decision.
